tips.comment: Ramon Di Loria won in March at 6f, then took on 3 lbs and could not follow up but was a decent third. I expect more today as he is back on turf where he won last August off a 60 and gets back to 6f today with handy Tommie Jakes in the saddle, claiming 3 lbs. He could bounce back.

INANNA has won three races from 5f to 7f. She was third over 6f at Thirsk on her latest outing earlier this month. The course, distance, and going should suit her. She seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.
Good stable, although inconsistent. This one's last win was over C/D. Good run last time out at Newcastle when 3rd, beaten 0.75 lengths by Tathmeen. Worth an interest at good odds.

Is getting on now, but has run well on the Aw @ Southwell last 3 runs and is a very well handicapped horse off today's dropping mark of 59. Is a C,D winner so return to turf not an issue, today's pilot is 75 percent here last 5 seasons and very shrewd trainer (does run a more fancied one in betting market here) 17 percent with a Lsp of 32.67 on his 4yo plus here last 5 seasons, making current 8/1 very good Ew value in the race.

White Umbrella hasn't been beaten by more than 2 lengths in 5 runs. Now 1lb below the last winning mark and gets stall 1 draw. Looks like the value pick of the race and has a big chance if making a good break from the stalls.

Royal Duke has had one win and three places over five furlongs. He is now attempting six furlongs for the first time. He has had the benefit of a recent run and could surprise if staying the extra furlong.
Ran well over the distance on his debut at Newcastle. Brings the best form to the table. Will be hard to beat today. Ground conditions today will suit. Stable going well.

In A Hurry was a good second on debut last June in a C5 at 7f. So we know she goes well when fresh and grabbed second in the final strides, which makes me think the move up to 1 mile today could give her enough time to do better.

Good stable, slow to mature but made a satisfactory debut this month. Slowly away and in the rear, outpaced 4 furlongs out. Kept on from 2 furlongs out under tender handling, finishing 4th beaten 6 lengths by Zowal. Improvement to come, worth an interest at good odds.

It's interesting that Paul Mulrennan takes over from apprentice Ami Waugh on Dwindling Funds, given the last-named is at the meeting. This horse ran green on debut and as an April foal is obviously a late developer. She may run better today for that experience and sneak into a place.
26,000 guineas yearling, well-bred out of Kameko. Stable has won the last two runnings of this race with newcomers. Worth an interest.

Spirit Of Acklam ran better than the result suggests at Doncaster, doing too much too soon on return over an inadequate mile. Stepping up to 10f at Ayr, where he has a strong record (two wins from three), looks a major plus. Easier company and race fitness now on side make him a big player.

Sea Regal is a strong contender in this race thanks to his previous good form and the fact that he returns after a break, which could have refreshed him. He has already won over this distance before, and his trainer, David O'Meara, often succeeds with horses coming back fresh. If he picks up where he left off last season and benefits from a manageable weight, Sea Regal could outclass his rivals in the final stretch.

The 4yo has 2 wins from 11. Lightly raced last year, struggled off a high mark but he was 3rd over this 10f C/D last summer off a 10lb higher mark. He had a wind op over the winter. Far too keen four weeks ago on the AW on his return from a 6 month break, and hampered late on when still in the mix. Worth another chance in this weak looking contest.
Good stable. This one had useful form in the 2022 season. Although he has shown little for a while, this is weak, and an improved run is not out of the question.
Good stable, inconsistent, and ran as if something was amiss when last seen in October. But this one won two of its 3 runs prior to that over C/D. Serious chance if back on song.

Samra Star could win this race thanks to her consistency and competitive handicap weight. Although her recent results are not outstanding, she has shown a good attitude in her runs and now drops slightly in class. At just four years old, she still has room for improvement, and Tommie Jakes’ ride could make the difference. If she secures a good position early on, she has serious chances to fight for the win.
Best runs of the year often come on the first run, and he needs to be at his best to show today. Well down the weights and with a 7lb claimer up, he can show up.
Won despite being slowly away and got up in the last half furlong with the field well spread out behind. Goes up 5lb here, which should not stop him winning again.

Slow away, at the back throughout, but made good headway to finish third over a mile at Redcar 7 days ago and will sharpen up for that run on the back of an absence of 193 days. He is a former course and distance winner who should be suited by this drop in trip.

Starliner last won in November off a 69 on the AW in a C4. A couple of weeks ago, he was a decent third on turf in a C4 off a 72, which makes me think that today's C5 off the same mark, with the rider claiming 5 lbs, could see him involved.

Seems to go best fresh, with his record following a break of at least 150 days reading 1-1-4-1. Reappearance win last year was his only victory but came from a mark of 77, and he's 3 lbs lower today. Draw looks ideal (stall 2), and today may be the time to catch him.

Good stable. Won twice in May/June last year before losing its form. Caught wide throughout the race when back to form last time out at Thirsk. Finished 2nd, beaten 2.25 lengths by Count Palatine. Could be well treated today.

Count Palatine had two wins in September, with the second of those being off a 73. Although a bit down the pack on the return a couple of weeks ago in a C4, he should come on for that run and is worth an EW 4P while running off a 74 and back in C5.

Orbital Chime returns today at Ayr after a six-month break, having shown promise with a third at Epsom and a fourth at Pontefract last autumn. Now racing off a mark of 72, just 1lb below his last winning rating, and back up to 7f, he could be primed for a strong run on seasonal reappearance.

She can perform much better than her last two efforts. But at least now, she is 6 lbs lighter than her last winning mark and also has course experience. She has the ability to bounce back strongly tomorrow.
City Of Strangers was eased towards the finish when still winning by 5L last time out on handicap debut. Although up 6 lbs for that, I think she could be bang in there again and defy the penalty.

Take an EW chance on 3yo irish filly Wee Mary here. She is still a maiden after 5 races but made a good step forward in this new season. Returns to turf today which should be good and she holds every chance to be in the mix here.
Crackinthunder has not been great in the three AW novice runs so far, but does drop to C6 for this handicap debut on a really low mark. Worth an EW from me, with Amie's 3 lbs claim to help as well.
This horse was placed last time from a 1 lb higher mark; ought to take plenty of beating in what looks like a worse race.

A dual-purpose horse who has run okay over hurdles without setting the world alight. Finished 7th last time at Pontefract when everything went wrong, and you can draw a line through that. But stepping up in distance could be a big positive.

Good stable. Won for this jockey over C/D last season. No show on its reappearance, but then not beaten far last time out at Wolverhampton, finishing 5th beaten 2.5 lengths by Rubelite. Looks well treated, serious chance.

Nearly two stones down the ratings and now steps up in trip which should suit. Now dropping into a 0-60 handicap and gets PJ for the first time. It is time to start winning and there is certainly a lot of potential for a successful season.

Outsider of the Party was 3rd of 5 last time out over 2 miles at Nottingham. Travelling best, it looked all over the winner 2 furlongs from home but found very little. A drop back to 1 mile 5 today should suit, and it is the least exposed of all of these. The 7/1 in a poor race looks decent.

Dual-purpose type whose last two runs over hurdles have been at 15.5-17f, so should get this staying trip pretty well. Last run on flat came in January over 8f at Newcastle, finishing last of 11, though has had three placed runs on flat on all-weather and on turf over 8-11.5f. Is running 4lb out of the handicap today, wears a tongue tie for the first time, and is having second run after a wind operation for trainer A. Nicol, who's saddled four winners from last 11 with a +LSP £3.75.

The stable had a surprise 11/1 winner yesterday. Although this one looks to have a hard task, he could surprise over the favored trip. He won twice at Wolverhampton over 14f off a high of 60 but was well beaten on return there over the same trip after 7 months off, never getting involved. He should strip fitter for that run, and if reverting to usual tactics of racing close up, could take this rise in trip off only 4lb more than the last win. Must not be held up for a run the first time over this trip.

DOUBLE THE TROUBLE was beaten two and a quarter lengths last time at Kempton, making it three placed results in a row. He won over C&D when last seen here in September and comes with huge claims that can help him make the difference by winning again.
Hollie Doyle takes over on board Diamondonthehill. Now it drops in class and is back up to its correct distance. Looks good to go close.

Tom Ward has served his apprenticeship abroad and in the UK with some of the big fish in the game, Mark Johnston, John Ferguson and Richard Hannon. He is not a household name and doesn't have a large string in his yard. He trains in Upper Lambourn and pops up with a winner here and there. Tom has a 25%(1 from 4) on the AW in the last 14 days thanks to his 15/2 winner yesterday. Tom reports that State Flag is in good form at home. She can run well fresh and hopefully she can keep the stable momentum going.

Diamondonthehill has a solid profile, but as a 7 year-old does not look particularly well handicapped. Rey De La Batalla, the four-year-old, bred and owned by Mr Moss, appears to be on the upgrade and has won over the course and distance twice including at this level. He was beaten by Diamondonthehill last time but was not well positioned out wide in the race. He is drawn low today and the weights remain unchanged, so could reverse the form. Signcastle City is interesting, if fit first time up.

This one is a 4-time winner from 6 to 8f, but all wins have come on turf. His only run on the A/W at Chelmsford, he was 7/11 over 7f, so he has something to prove on debut here. He won 3 from 8 last year but has been off for 8 months and drops to 7f, but 1 grade lower and could get involved.
One of only three course and distance winners in the race and has gone close from today's mark on its last two AW starts; can do so once more.
Second beaten favorite last time. Distance no problem. Good jockey and trainer. Will be at the business end of the race. NAP WIN.

A winner the only prior time that he ran in a Class 4 over C&D back in September. He is only a couple of pounds higher here and won with more than that in hand. Shaped well enough in a couple of Class 2 events in the spring and will appreciate the drop in class.

While the two market principals are respected on form, they lack a recent race. Whereas, Rockit Tommy ran as well as could have been expected on seasonal return at Newbury over a slightly inadequate 10 furlongs. He had a very good season last year, winning twice in this grade over a mile and a half on the all-weather and should be sharper today. Appier rates a danger after dropping in the weights.

Found a very hot class 4 over C/D too much for them Lto, but going to be back @ home @ this level and they are 55 percent here @ Lingfield. Interesting jockey booking today for this stable and shrewd trainer does well with his Aw runners in general, making current 35/1 worth Ew consideration here.

Go Go Boots returns to Lingfield today after a smooth debut win over a mile here in December. She steps up to 1m2f and carries a 7lb penalty, but her Oaks entry and pedigree suggest she’s got plenty more to offer.

LKARAMA has been placed in one race from two starts, second over 7f at Wolverhampton on his latest outing earlier this month. The course, distance, and surface should suit, and he could well be able to go one better and win this race.

Owen Burrows' trained filly makes an appeal on her American pedigree, being by American Pharoah out of smart scorer up to 10f Vale Dori (by Asiatic Boy), as well as a half-sister to US 1m turf winner Mizzyaan.
A good run on debut to finish 2nd behind a promising rival. He's closely related to an AW winner so expected to take well to this surface and can get his nose in front here.

Just Ten High lines up today at Lingfield after a solid second over course and distance last week. He returns quickly off the same mark of 62, with Jim Crowley back in the saddle. Looks well placed to go one better.
Stayed on well over this trip at Wolverhampton 9 days ago and 7th of 12 but only beaten 3.75 lengths. Likely to come late here too with the downhill finish aiding that momentum.

Just Ten High is quickly turned out before the official handicapper can reassess his runner-up effort last time. He is thrice a beaten favourite off a mark of 62, and 5/4 makes limited appeal. Libra Tiger has, on the other hand, been quietly sliding down the weights and has responded well to cheekpieces in his last two races, including on seasonal return last time. He is taken to give the jolly a run for his money.

Fresh has been the time to catch him so far in his career, winning a Class 5 over C&D on his opening start last season. He is 4lb higher here but he won that by more than three lengths so there is plenty of wiggle room in this rating.
Another horse to have dropped down the weights like a stone, from a mark in the 90s down to 66 for today. The booking of Jim Crowley catches the eye, and the market has shown a positive response.

No show on turf Lto, but this course winner going to be more @ home back here @ Lingfield on Aw. Was only just beaten off today's mark @ Wolverhamtpon 4 runs back, good apprentice retains ride taking off 3lb and shrewd trainer does well on the Aw, making current 8/1 solid Ew value in the race.
One win from 34 is a bit of a concern but stats show that Francesi has been placed in 13 of those races and the grey kept on well off a pound higher last time out.

good stable, improved form since being fitted with a tongue tie, winning over C/D and finnishing placed three times, last time out finishing 4th at Kempton, keeping on well final furlong, beaten 2 lengths by Port Erin, worth an interest back at this track

King Cabo was quite well supported on seasonal return last time at Kempton, but caught a handicap blot and had no chance. He has been consistently running in better races than this since winning last August off today's mark and gets on well with his 7-pound claiming pilot. They are fitting a tongue strap to King Cabo today, and that might well bring out an extra few pounds of performance if effective. Draw 1 is a bonus.
Fresh from a comfortable win at Bath off this same mark of 68, Darvel now switches to Polytrack in similar company. With fitness and form firmly in his favour, he looks set to strike again.

I had this race between Cupola and this one with preference just for Camera Shy with Oisin Murphy booked. As a 2yo he won a class 2 novice race before being sent off odds on in Group company in Italy which speaks volumes. He was slow away in that race and hampered when making ground but the fact he was sent off at 4/6 clearly shows they think he's better than a handicapper. He's racing here off just 72 and looks to hold a major chance.

Nothing special in three 2yo runs last year when at the Varian yard, but returned 4 weeks ago for a new trainer and made quite the impression on handicap debut to come a 3/4l 2nd to hot favorite Kamekist, with both well clear of 3rd. That was on the AW at Wolves, so will need to transfer that form to turf today and if so, has a decent chance.
Although this is first run in couple months for Cupola she still had good rating last time around therefore i fancy her to be productive enough to atleast cover handicap tonight.

I am hoping we will start seeing the best of her now handicapping. She will need to make some improvements from her last time out effort when she finished 7th of 10 at Southwell last November. Sometimes, switching from AW to turf can be beneficial.
Needed her reappearance run last time. Comes here from a falling mark, down to 69, and did run well on nursery debut last October from a mark of 75, so looks potentially well in.

As only six and a half lengths behind Shadow of Light at Newmarket on August 24, best run so far. Early days with this well-bred type, but that's fairly good form as Shadow has won twice in G1 company since. Each way providing for first run after break.

FORTELEZA is forgiven for the last time out run as a 2-year-old as it was on the heavy ground at Haydock. I'll give her a look based on the run before that at Redcar, which was a near miss and on firmer ground and from only a pound lower in the weights. She hasn't run for over six months, but the stable does OK with them fresh. As she probably makes more progress at some point this season, I'll back her whilst she's this big a price.

Trainer Richard Hughes remains in good form and Sea Founder the 3yo son of Sea The Moon has the pedigree to win a race of this nature. Oisin Murphy is a significant booking and the market suggests he will be hard to beat.

Bondi Beach is probably going to be more popular than this horse after a very ordinary debut, but there were a few excuses to be offered for that debut failure, not the least of which was drawing wide on a course that favors inside barriers. Was forward for a long way despite that and faded late. Needed the experience, and I'm expecting a much-improved showing this time out.
Twice-raced gelding who has not shown much ability in the two starts to date. But hoping he has trained well in the seven months post those efforts, and the drop down in class should help.
No price at all but Tycoon looks to break his maiden tag and it will be a shock if this son of Kingman doesn't do just that.
It is about time R Beckett's yard started to kick in. Eddie Greaterex rides well for him, and he is on Glazia in this. It looks a player on breeding, so keep an eye on the betting.

Considering the sire, I saw enough from the LTO effort that gives me some hope that this horse can build on the LTO effort. Given the stability of running the same distance and also being helped by dropping down 3 classes.

Promethean lines up today at Windsor after a luckless run in the Spring Mile at Doncaster, where he was hampered yet still finished seventh in a big field. Now stepping up to 1m2f, a trip that should suit, he looks poised to deliver a big performance.
This 5 year old horse has shown some great previously with having finished second most recently therefore i fanxy him to be productive tonight aswell and make yet another decent run.

Can go well fresh as proved last year when winning this race, so would expect a decent run. I was disappointed with a couple of runs last year with inexperienced jockeys making errors and made note that will do better with a pro jockey on top, which we get today. Going not ideal is a possible negative, but although preference for some cut, does appear to run okay on any surface.

16/1 looks way too big for this horse, which saves his best for this track with a 2 from 4 record over C&D. Those were on similarly fast ground off 73 and were easy wins, so he is capable of winning this off 78 with the stable's useful 3lb claiming apprentice booked. He'll strip fitter after the seasonal debut run last time out, and a return to Windsor could be the key here.

The in-form James Owen trains Kinetic, who did the biz last time out, winning a Class 5 12f Fillies' Handicap off a mark of 68 by 11¼ lengths. Put up 5 lbs to a mark of 63, but the excellent young apprentice jockey Mason Paetel has been booked and steals 7 lbs off his back, leaving him 2 lbs better off for his last win. The 4-year-old Kodiac filly is hard to oppose in this moderate Class 5 handicap over 1m 3f 99y.
A modest run on her seasonal return 7/8 at Yarmouth, but worth noting that her previous four runs included a win and 3 places. She looks to be off a fair mark and offers each-way potential.

The 7-year-old mare wasn’t great last year for her new yard, but she was only beaten around a length last August. She ran quite a few nice races as a 4-year-old and 5-year-old, including on quick ground, and her racing mark now is around 20 lb lower. She had a 6-month break, and I’ll take a chance that the trainer has fixed any problems.

Cherry Cola dropsback to her ideal trip after struggling over hurdles, she returns to a track where she’s a dual winner and now sits 6lb below her last winning mark. With a 5lb claim boosting her appeal, she’s primed for a big run.

Showed only limited ability last season in three starts for a mark but he is bred to be much better than this opening mark of 59. The horses that finished around him in those runs suggest that this mark is more than workable. He has been gelded ahead of his handicap debut and it's interesting that powerful connections have persisted with him.
Caught the eye on his last run of the season when given a tender ride. Would have needed his reappearance run last time and comes here 2 lb lower with new headgear applied.

Blackbrook makes his handicap debut today at Windsor after showing improvement with a fourth at Kempton. Opening off a workable mark of 53 against exposed rivals, and with a strong jockey booking, he looks ready to step forward.
Beaten 3L off 60 over 7f at Kempton last time. Top course jockey Tom Marquand is a notable booking. Up in trip, good mark on best 2-year-old form. Interesting.

Excellent sire form 'Invincible Army' shows a 31% win rate as a 2-year-old, whopping 50% win rate in 3-year-old events, with a combined overall 38% win rate. Second time on the turf. Recent second at Wolverhampton, horse finished third, won easily on good/firm going at Bath Course. Should be in the places here, with sire form and first run on turf with new ownership.

Bang On The Bell heads to Windsor in good form and looks a big player dropping into Class 5 company. Last time out, he finished a strong second at Wolverhampton, just behind Cinque Verde, the 4/1 joint-favourite, in a race rated 10lbs higher than tomorrow’s contest. That was a clear sign he’s still competitive at a higher level. Two starts ago, he also ran well at Chelmsford in a Class 4 handicap, beaten only 2.75 lengths. Now slipping down to a mark of 68, having been as high as 86 just last November, he’s very well treated at the weights. The step back into slightly calmer waters should suit him perfectly, and with conditions in his favour, he looks a cracking each-way bet at 8/1. Good Luck!

Came from off the pace to win at Lingfield and ran on well when challenged for the lead. A couple of years ago, this horse was a class 2 to class 3 horse. Last time out was a class 6, which it won, and should be able to cope with this class 5. My rating for Harry Brown is 57.2, followed by Bang on the Bell 55.4 and Torfrida 54.6. It's a tight race like a lot of sprints, but HB showed very willing LTO, and that counts for a lot in my book. Good luck.

SECRET HANDSHAKE will benefit from the return to turf and could well get involved if performing to the levels of last season's campaign. Only two pounds above last winning mark and only one click above a promising run at Sandown at the end of August. The last two all-weather runs have served to tune up for the turf season, so this one could fare better now.

4yo filly Tiger Tulip is back on a handy mark just 1lb above his last winning mark from October 23. Should be a lot sharper today on 2nd run after a 5 month break. Booking of Silvestre De Sousa a good move and shouldn't be far away here.

This horse has run several excellent races at Windsor off marks in and around its current mark (58). It has won off 57 and been second off 58. It had a good seasonal opener at Nottingham when fading in the final furlong to finish last, not beaten far.

The trainer of this horse isn't known for having a good strike rate, so it's certainly interesting that he appears to target this course with 5 of his last 23 runners here winning. That's an impressive stat, and he's even booked a jockey who rides the course really well too (he's won 4 of his last 14 at the course). The horse's best run was when 2nd over a similarly fast ground 5 furlongs, when getting within a length of a horse that won his next race off 80. BTR races here off 57, and at the prices, could be worth a little interest.
Hasn't won since November 2023 but has been a runner-up in 5 of his 10 outings since then, including last time out at Southwell. On a very competitive mark.
This horse loves Wolverhampton. Last time out it stayed on strongly to finish fourth and the time before it won. You can forget its run at Beverley last time and look back at its record here.

Senseofentitlement was lightly raced last year after leaving David O'Mara, and there are reasons for performances that apparently offered little encouragement. But as a consequence, he has dropped to a mark of 51, six pounds less than his last win over the course and distance. The jockey is the part-owner, and he might well run better than expected back at this track.
Gordon Norse is back at Wolverhampton after a tidy debut third over this trip. Looks a big player in an easier race and should be in the mix.

I Follow Rivers heads to Wolverhampton today after a promising third on handicap debut. He now drops into a Class 6 over 7f, racing off a mark of 52. With a favourable draw and a competitive field, he looks well-placed to build on that effort.
Did win a 7-furlong race on the Tapeta as a 2-year-old. This is the first time back at this distance. Ran okay after a break latest and should be spot on this evening for a good run.

This horse has been placed on its last 2 AW starts at today's 7f trip. In a race that looks very uncompetitive beyond the top 2 in the betting, it ought to have more than enough to place (at least) again.
Sharon Curly looks to be in the mix as he is down in grade and getting the extra distance to make it at a less competitive level.
Mythical Bird sets the standard for me by being second in a C2 novice when last out. She should find today's C5 a tad easier with the expected competition returning from a break as well.
Newcomer who looks to have a very good pedigree and bred to win races such as this one. An obvious market check is recommended to view where the money is going.

Was slowly away on turf debut as a 2yo last season @ Newbury, but did stay on very well to come 5/11 beaten 12.5 lengths in a class 4 maiden over over 7f. Nice pedigree which is related to numerous winners suggests that today's extended 1.1 miles will suit on 3yo return, very under used jockey up and shrewd trainer is 36 percent with his 3yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 20/1 solid Ew value in the race.

HENRY HAWK has won four races at 5f. Seventh over 5f at Musselburgh on his latest outing earlier this month. Course, distance, and surface should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.
This horse returned to form with a 2nd place at the track last time. It's a course and distance winner, and in a modest race, can place at least.

MAY REMAIN is the other to consider in this one. One of the older horses, but these sorts are worth backing when they are in good shape. The yard gives him another quick spin after the near miss here last time out. Stays at the same weight too.
Her latest two wins have both been over course and distance. The 5 lbs increase might not be enough to stop her gaining a seventh career win here.
Kipp Kelly disappointed at Newcastle but had excuses and had gone close in better company prior. Now down to 45 and back over 6f at Wolverhampton, he looks weighted to get involved.

If you persevere with RED WALLS, you will hit eventually, and you'd still be staying competitive if you backed on each and every one of his 105 runs to date. He has won here five times and can still perform over this sprint distance. He has a tendency to pop in when least expected, so is given a whirl at this price and this reduced mark. The pace profile and draw don't look bad either.

Out of her depth when finishing down the field in a Listed Event when last seen in November last year. But she returns on a very attractive looking mark on her first start for an in-form yard and could have too much class for this field. She wasn't beaten far over today's C&D in a Class 3 Handicap back in October last year when finishing 4th of 12 to 'Aramram'. On that run, she must surely take a lot of beating off a 2lb lower mark.

Remains consistent despite being 8 years old in these sprints. Proved that when returning from a 4-month break and winning a competitive sprint on the turf. That run should put him spot on for today, and despite a 1 lb rise in the weights, he remains competitive based on his previous CD form.

Course and distance winner who was last seen at Kempton 30 days ago where finishing 9th/12 however that was his return run after a 203 day break and he did look in need of the run now with that outing under his belt he arrives here in a much fitter state and is now operating back on a very handy mark of 86 that being 2lb below his last winning mark making him a very serious contender in a suitable looking assignment that also represents a drop in class back down to class 4 company jockey Luke Morris takes the ride on Tom Clover's Dark Angel gelding and he is more than capable of bouncing back here must enter calculations

Not the best strike rate with only two wins from 23 runs but has run plenty of good races in defeat as shown by cominng in the top 3 on 7 other occasions. Joined Ivan Furtado from Roger Varian and he's had three runs for him so far and although his first two were very below par in November and December last year before he was then put away before returning for his seasonal debut at Pontefract this month. He returned with a much better run (albeit finishing 6th of 10) he still ran much better than his previous couple and that was in a decent C2 race, which should bring him on nicely fitness wise for this return to the AW and the drop into C4 company with Billy Loughnane booked so looks to have a good chance.
